- `POST /api/admin/users` is admin-only. It rejects a supplied ID, then checks normalized login and case-insensitive email for duplicates (`UserResource.java:105-117`).
- It delegates to transactional `UserService.createUser`—the service class is `@Transactional` (`UserService.java:30-32`). The method normalizes fields, generates password/reset credentials, activates the account, resolves authorities, saves it, and evicts login/email caches (`UserService.java:142-174`; cache keys/eviction at `UserService.java:310-314`).
- Repository lookup caches are defined for authority-bearing login/email reads (`UserRepository.java:18-33`).
- After `createUser` returns, the controller invokes asynchronous creation email, then constructs `201 Created`, `Location`, alert headers, and the persisted entity body (`UserResource.java:118-122`). Email rendering and delivery occur asynchronously (`MailService.java:89-112`), and delivery exceptions are only logged (`MailService.java:69-81`).

**Boundary risks:** The duplicate checks occur outside the service transaction and are separate from `save`, creating a check-then-insert race; concurrent requests can both pass and only a database uniqueness constraint can arbitrate (`UserResource.java:113-118`, `UserService.java:171`). The service transaction completes before the controller schedules email, so persistence/cache eviction, email, and HTTP response are not one atomic unit (`UserService.java:30-32,171-174`; `UserResource.java:118-122`). Consequently, the user can commit but email submission/delivery can fail while the request still returns `201`; asynchronous mail failures are swallowed as warnings (`MailService.java:79-81,109-112`). Cache eviction also executes before transaction commit, permitting another thread to repopulate a cache from pre-commit database state (`UserService.java:171-172,310-314`).
